unit.label: Recent routines, useful expressions & permission
unit.title: Can I Go Check It Out?
unit.description: 10 new words and forms, with 每天 and 剛開始 reviewed from Unit 22. Talk about recent activities and ask, grant, or refuse permission.

goal.pinyin: Wǒ kě bù kěyǐ qù kàn bǐsài?
goal.meaning: May I go watch the game?

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 7, pp. 135–145. Remaining dialogue vocabulary and permission use of 可以; original Hanzi Steps examples and exercises.

lessons.title: Lately, Every Day
lessons.subtitle: Finish the routine vocabulary from this lesson.

steps.prompt: Which word means “recently; lately”?
steps.explanation: 最近 means recently or lately.

steps.prompt: Which expression means “every day”?
steps.explanation: 每天 combines 每 with 天 to mean every day.

steps.prompt: Someone says 我最近很忙. Must this mean “I am busy every day”?
options: No. 最近 says lately, not every day.
Yes. 最近 and 每天 mean the same thing.
steps.answer: No. 最近 says lately, not every day.
steps.explanation: 最近 identifies a recent period; 每天 explicitly means every day.

lessons.title: Wait a Moment
lessons.subtitle: Say you will do something later or that you are occupied.

steps.prompt: A friend asks whether you are free tonight. Which answer says you have something to do?
steps.explanation: 有事 means you have something to take care of.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 等 is děng, the first character of 等一下.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 事 is shì, the second character of 有事.

steps.prompt: Your friend says 等一下. What are they asking you to do?
steps.explanation: 等 is wait; 一下 makes it a brief wait.

lessons.title: Writing Characters
lessons.subtitle: Talk about beginning to write and finding it interesting.

steps.prompt: Which expression means “to write characters”?
steps.explanation: 寫字 is the familiar verb 寫 plus the newly taught noun 字.

steps.prompt: Which sentence says you just started writing characters?
steps.explanation: 剛開始 marks that something has just begun.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 字 is zì: written character; word.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 意 is yì: idea; meaning.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 思 is sī: think; thought.

lessons.title: Ask the Teacher
lessons.subtitle: Use 問 and review a softened repeated action.

steps.prompt: What does 問 mean?
steps.explanation: 問 means to ask.

steps.prompt: Why is 問 repeated in 問問?
options: It makes the action sound lighter or more tentative.
It changes 問 into a noun.
steps.answer: It makes the action sound lighter or more tentative.
steps.explanation: This reuses the softened action pattern taught earlier.

steps.prompt: You need to ask the teacher something briefly. Which uses the softened action correctly?
steps.explanation: Repeat 問 itself, leaving 老師 outside the repeated verb.

lessons.title: You May Do It
lessons.subtitle: Use 可以 to grant permission, not just possibility.

steps.prompt: In this unit, what does 可以 express in 你可以在這裡寫字?
steps.explanation: Here 可以 means that the action is permitted.

steps.prompt: A host says 你可以在這裡喝咖啡. What does 可以 do here?
steps.explanation: The host is allowing the activity; 可以 is not a command.

lessons.title: May I? / You May Not
lessons.subtitle: Ask for permission and say an action is not allowed.

steps.prompt: Which form says the action is not permitted?
steps.explanation: 不可以 is the negative permission form.

steps.prompt: Which two forms can ask for permission?
options: 可不可以 and 可以嗎
steps.answer: 可不可以 and 可以嗎
steps.explanation: Both question forms can be used to ask whether an action is allowed.

steps.prompt: Photos are prohibited here. Which reply refuses permission?
options: 你可不可以在這裡照相？
steps.explanation: 不可以 refuses permission. 可以 allows it, and 可不可以 asks a question.

steps.prompt: Which is a standard permission question using A-not-A?
options: 我可不可以在這裡寫字？
我可不可以在這裡寫字嗎？
steps.answer: 我可不可以在這裡寫字？
steps.explanation: Choose the A-not-A construction or the 嗎 construction; do not combine them here.

lessons.title: Unit 23 Review
lessons.subtitle: Recent routines, useful expressions, writing, and permission.

steps.prompt: Choose the permission question.
steps.explanation: 可不可以 asks whether the action is permitted.

steps.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I have something to do tonight.”
steps.explanation: 有事 means being occupied with something.

steps.prompt: You want permission to sing here. Which asks for it?
steps.explanation: 可以…嗎 asks whether the action is allowed; the other sentences report a preference or routine.

steps.prompt: The teacher says 你不可以在這裡喝咖啡. Are you allowed to drink coffee here?
steps.explanation: 不可以 prohibits the action.

steps.prompt: Which expresses interest in writing, rather than having something to do?
steps.explanation: 有意思 means interesting. 有事 means being occupied; 等一下 asks someone to wait.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 字 is zì: written character; word.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 意 is yì: idea; meaning.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 思 is sī: think; thought.

steps.prompt: A host is allowing you to drink tea here. Which sentence grants that permission?
steps.explanation: 可以 grants permission; 不可以 prohibits it, and the last sentence asks about an action.

newVocabulary.meaning: wait a moment; in a little while
to have something to do; be occupied

字.note: 字 is fourth-tone zì. Here it means a written Chinese character, as in 寫字.
字.memory: A three-stroke roof 宀 sits over the three-stroke 子. Keep the child component centered under the roof.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: The first three strokes form the roof across the top of 字.

parts.label: 子
parts.name: child component
parts.description: The last three strokes form 子 beneath the roof, ending with the long horizontal.

等.note: 等 is third-tone děng. In 等一下 it means to wait a moment or do something a little later.
等.memory: The six-stroke bamboo top 𥫗 sits over 寺. Think of waiting under the paired bamboo marks.

parts.label: 𥫗
parts.name: bamboo top
parts.description: The first six strokes form the paired bamboo component across the top.

parts.label: 寺
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 寺 underneath the bamboo top.

事.note: 事 is fourth-tone shì. 有事 literally means to have a matter to deal with, so it often means being occupied.
事.memory: The middle box and hand-like strokes are crossed by a final vertical hook. Keep the whole eight-stroke form compact.

parts.label: main
parts.name: upper and middle frame
parts.description: The first seven strokes build the top line, central 口-like box, and hand-shaped middle.

parts.label: 亅
parts.name: final hook
parts.description: The eighth stroke is the long central vertical hook that locks the form together.

example.meaning: have something to do; be occupied

意.note: 意 is fourth-tone yì. In 有意思, it combines with 思 to describe something as interesting or engaging.
意.memory: 音 fills the upper nine strokes and 心 forms the four-stroke base. Keep the heart component broad enough to support the top.

parts.label: 音
parts.name: sound component
parts.description: The first nine strokes form 音 at the top of 意.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 心 across the bottom.

思.note: 思 is normally read sī on its own; in 意思 the second syllable is commonly neutral: yìsi.
思.memory: 田 forms the five-stroke top and 心 forms the four-stroke bottom. Keep the heart slightly wider than the box above.

parts.label: 田
parts.name: field component
parts.description: The first five strokes form the square 田 at the top.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 心 under 田.

u23-permission-keyi.title: Permission with 可以
u23-permission-keyi.explanation: 可以 was already used earlier for possibility. In this lesson it also grants permission: the speaker says an action is allowed. As an auxiliary verb, 可以 comes before the action.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ xiě zì.

examples.meaning: You may go watch the game.

u23-permission-keyi.remember: Permission 可以 comes before the action it allows.

u23-permission-negative.title: Not permitted: 不可以
u23-permission-negative.explanation: 不可以 says an action is not permitted. Here 不可以 expresses permission/prohibition rather than the earlier possibility sense of 可以.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ chànggē.
Nǐ bù kěyǐ qù kàn bǐsài.
examples.meaning: You are not allowed to go watch the game.

u23-permission-negative.remember: 不可以 = not allowed / may not.

u23-permission-questions.title: Ask permission
u23-permission-questions.pattern: 可不可以 + VP? / 可以 + VP + 嗎?
u23-permission-questions.explanation: To ask whether an action is permitted, use 可不可以 before the action, or use 可以 before the action and add 嗎 at the end. In other contexts the A-not-A form can also ask about possibility; here the situation makes the permission reading clear.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kě bù kěyǐ qù kàn bǐsài?
examples.meaning: May I go watch the game?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ qù kàn bǐsài ma?
examples.meaning: May I go watch the game?

u23-permission-questions.remember: Use either 可不可以 + action or 可以 + action + 嗎. Do not add 嗎 to the A-not-A question taught here.

u23-recent-busy.meaning: I have been very busy lately.
u23-recent-busy.note: 最近 locates the situation in the recent period.

u23-everyday-class.note: 每天 sets the repeated time; 都 links the repeated set to the activity.

u23-wait.note: 一下 makes the request/action bounded and light.

u23-have-business.meaning: I have something to do tonight.
u23-have-business.note: 有事 is a common way to say you are occupied.

u23-just-started.note: 剛開始 introduces something that has only just begun.

u23-interesting.pinyin: Wǒ juéde xiě zì hěn yǒu yìsi.
u23-interesting.meaning: I think writing characters is interesting.
u23-interesting.note: 有意思 describes something as interesting or engaging.

u23-ask-teacher.meaning: I want to ask the teacher.
u23-ask-teacher.note: 問問 repeats the action verb to make the action sound lighter/tentative.

u23-ask.note: 問 directly takes the person being asked.

u23-may-write.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ xiě zì.
u23-may-write.note: Context makes 可以 permission: the action is allowed.

u23-may-watch.meaning: You may go watch the game.
u23-may-watch.note: 可以 precedes the permitted action.

u23-may-not-sing.pinyin: Nǐ bù kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ chànggē.
u23-may-not-sing.note: 不可以 prohibits the following action.

u23-can-i-game.pinyin: Wǒ kě bù kěyǐ qù kàn bǐsài?
u23-can-i-game.meaning: May I go watch the game?
u23-can-i-game.note: 可不可以 is the A-not-A permission question.

u23-can-i-game-ma.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ qù kàn bǐsài ma?
u23-can-i-game-ma.meaning: May I go watch the game?
u23-can-i-game-ma.note: The statement frame keeps 可以 before the action and adds 嗎 at the end.

u23-busy-afternoon.text: 我最近每天下午都很忙。
u23-busy-afternoon.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn měitiān xiàwǔ dōu hěn máng.
u23-busy-afternoon.meaning: Lately I have been busy every afternoon.
u23-busy-afternoon.note: 最近 gives the recent period; 每天下午 says the routine repeats every afternoon.

u23-writing-evaluation.pinyin: Nǐ juéde xiě zì yǒu yìsi ma?
u23-writing-evaluation.meaning: Do you think writing characters is interesting?
u23-writing-evaluation.note: 有意思 evaluates the activity; the final 嗎 makes this a yes/no question.

u23-permitted-coffee.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ hē kāfēi.
u23-permitted-coffee.note: A host grants permission to drink coffee in this place.

u23-photo-permission.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ zhàoxiàng ma?
u23-photo-permission.note: You are asking the person responsible for this place whether photos are allowed.
